title: Suspended or barred, and what they had been paid without competition
question: Of the firms and organizations the City later suspended or barred from contracting, which had been paid under rules that set competition aside?
finding: 10 firms and organizations named on the City’s suspension and debarment lists appear in the payment file, paid $126.4 million between them since fiscal 2019. 1 of them received $100,000 or more under rules that set competition aside, $40.5 million in all; the largest is Providence Foundation Of San Francisco ($40.4 million, emergency powers; bidding waived by ordinance; Health Department sole-source list). Payments issued in fiscal years after the year of the action add up to $11.9 million.
how: Business and organization names were taken from the City’s current list of suspended and debarred contractors and from the Controller’s twelve semi-annual reports (December 2020 to June 2026), and matched by exact normalized name to payees in the vendor-payment file. The action date is the effective date the report gives, or the date of the suspension order, or else the date of the first report that lists the name. A payment counts as after the action when the fiscal year it was issued in, read from its voucher number, is later than the fiscal year of the action; the latest year paid is read the same way. Individuals are not matched.
limits: Name match. A suspension is not a finding of wrongdoing: several are pending a criminal case or a hearing, one hearing officer ruled a suspension unwarranted, and one matter ended in a settlement. Payments after the action date can be for work done before it, which the City still owes. Being paid without competition did not cause the later action and the two facts are shown together only because both are exceptions to the ordinary rules. The payment file labels each line with a fiscal year that is not always the year the payment was issued: some earlier payments, mostly on purchase orders in multi-year capital funds, are filed under a later year, and the Controller's own published figures follow that label. Payments are dated here by voucher number, a single running sequence, which moves $5.52 billion of $119.3 billion (4.6%) to an earlier year than its label; $1.08 billion of that belongs to fiscal 2018 or earlier, before the file starts. Near the turn of a year the number dates a payment to within a few days. Payments that belong to fiscal 2018 or earlier are in none of the figures here.
